title: Reproduce the exact Ramsey number R(3,3)=6
statement: Show that every red/blue coloring of the unordered edges of K6 contains a monochromatic triangle, and exhibit a red/blue coloring of K5 without one. Produce an independently checkable finite certificate alongside a human-readable proof.
source_locator: DS1.18 section 2.1(a,d); Kiem–Pokutta–Spiegel section 1 identifies R(3,3)=6.
status_basis: Established theorem cited by the current dynamic survey and the inspected research paper. This is a proposed reproduction, not a new open problem.
plain_summary: A tiny, established graph-coloring theorem makes a transparent starting benchmark for testing future search-to-certificate workflows.
assumptions: Finite simple undirected complete graphs; no loops or multiple edges.
Exactly one of two available colors is assigned to each unordered pair; either color may be unused.
A triangle consists of three distinct vertices; all three edges must share the same color.
scope: Known-result reproduction at five and six vertices only. Any success is a calibration result, not new mathematics or evidence of competence on open Ramsey cases.
target: Produce both the lower-bound witness and universal upper-bound argument, plus a reproducible exact certificate format.
success_criteria: Supply an edge list or adjacency encoding for a valid five-vertex witness.
Give a logically complete proof for all six-vertex colorings.
If enumeration is used, account for all 2^15 colorings with an explicit encoding/completeness argument and independently checked triangle witnesses.
Record future tools, versions, logs, and human interventions; do not infer a general AI success rate from this one result.
known_results: R(3,3)=6 is an established result, cited in SRC-MATH-014 section 1; SRC-MATH-001 section 2.1 discusses its history and critical graphs.
significance: Low novelty, high workflow value: it tests statement translation, lower versus upper bounds, exact enumeration, and auditable evidence on a case humans can inspect.

relations.explanation: Shares edge-coloring/certificate concepts, but the four-color research problem has vastly larger search and proof costs.

requirements.data: No external data required; source metadata and generated certificates only.
requirements.compute: Estimated ordinary laptop CPU and modest memory for a future run. The full six-vertex space has 32,768 colorings; this is a combinatorial size, not a measured runtime or budget.
requirements.theoretical_assumptions: Ordinary finite combinatorics; a future formal proof must state any axioms and encoding lemmas.

obstacles: Off-by-one confusion between the Ramsey threshold and witness size.
A passing checker cannot establish universal coverage unless the enumeration is proved complete.
Memorized proof reproduction is not evidence of novel reasoning.

steps: Human reviewer matches graph/color definitions to the literature statement.
Check every triangle of the five-vertex witness using an independent implementation.
Review the upper-bound proof directly; if computational, verify the enumeration map and all emitted certificates.
If formalized, compare the formal theorem and assumptions to this exact statement.
validation.human_review_difficulty: Low for mathematical reasoning; moderate only if the implementation hides enumeration or certificate assumptions.
validation.statement_alignment: Both R(3,3)>5 and R(3,3)<=6 are required. A single good coloring or tests on sampled colorings cannot establish equality.

known_attempts: The current Ramsey survey records established treatments; this project has performed no reproduction.
unresolved_checks: Choose future certificate serialization and checker language.
Decide whether formal proof is desired in addition to a short human proof.
No runtime, cost, success-rate, or model comparison data exist yet.
